text.paragraph: New patient visit for about three months of tiredness, weight loss, darkening skin, nausea and back ache, with blood tests and urgent endocrinology referral. Concerns: She has felt worn out for months and is losing weight, and her face and hands have darkened; she wants to know what is wrong; She wants enough energy to finish the novel she is revising and to walk out again. [S]

tr.td: New patient visit for about three months of tiredness, weight loss, darkening skin, nausea and back ache, with blood tests and urgent endocrinology referral
Endocrinology consultation with a cosyntropin stimulation test, diagnosis, and start of replacement
Two-week review after starting replacement: electrolytes, cause, and autoimmune screening
Six-week review: electrolytes, renin, blood count, and recovery
Seven-month review: replacement, renin, thyroid, mood, and the closing of the differential
Same-day sick visit for streptococcal pharyngitis with stress dosing of hydrocortisone

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Initial evaluation of tiredness, weight loss, darkening skin, low sodium and high potassium: blood count, metabolic panel, thyroid tests, ferritin, vitamin B12 and folate at the first visit; urgent 8 am cortisol and ACTH with a cosyntropin stimulation test within days; until then, salt freely, and go to the emergency department at once for vomiting, fainting, confusion or severe abdominal pain
Urgent endocrinology consultation within three days to confirm or exclude primary adrenal insufficiency, start replacement if confirmed, and plan the search for the cause

Replacement: hydrocortisone 10 mg on waking and 5 mg at 2 pm (15 mg a day) and fludrocortisone 0.1 mg each morning, adjusted by weight, energy, blood pressure lying and standing, salt craving and signs of over- or under-replacement, with sodium, potassium and plasma renin after any fludrocortisone change and at least yearly

Written sick-day rules (double the hydrocortisone for fever above 38 °C, triple it above 39 °C, and inject 100 mg and call 911 for vomiting, inability to take tablets, or feeling faint), an emergency hydrocortisone injection kit with training, a steroid emergency card and a medical ID, reviewed at every visit

Cause and differential: 21-hydroxylase antibodies at the two-week visit; adrenal CT and tuberculosis testing only if they are negative; examination for lymph nodes and spleen, LDH and a chest X-ray now, with CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis if weight loss, fevers, night sweats or enlarged nodes persist once replacement is established

Screening for associated autoimmune disease: TSH (normal at intake) at least yearly; vitamin B12, A1c, and celiac serology with total IgA; ask about periods at each visit and check FSH if they become irregular or stop
Anemia: ferritin, vitamin B12 and folate at intake; repeat the blood count on treatment and look further only if it does not recover

Streptococcal pharyngitis: amoxicillin 500 mg twice daily for ten days; hydrocortisone doubled under the sick-day rules until a day without fever and then back to the usual dose; fluids with salt; the emergency injection with a 911 call if she vomits or cannot take tablets; neck nodes rechecked at the six-week visit
A diagnosis within one week of the first visit, with treatment started the same day if adrenal insufficiency is confirmed
Cosyntropin test three days after the first visit; replacement started the same day
No adrenal crisis and no emergency admission through the episode
No crisis or admission; one febrile illness managed at home with stress dosing
Sodium and potassium normal, renin in the upper normal range, and no postural drop by the six-week visit
Sodium 139 and potassium 4.4 mmol/L; renin 3.4 ng/mL/h; no postural drop
She can state the sick-day rules and give the emergency injection by the two-week visit
Stated the rules and gave a practice injection on a trainer
Weight back to her usual 57 kg, and energy for full mornings of writing, by six months
Weight 57.2 kg from 52.0; writing full mornings and walking several miles

list.item: Independent in all activities; tires after a short walk and needs to rest in the afternoon; has cut her writing time from full mornings to an hour or two [S]
